messaging.title: Messaging
messaging.intro: Where email and text messages go, and what signing in requires. These can also be set from the deployment environment; anything saved here replaces it.
messaging.protectionIntro: Documents attached to a protected cave are always served — they are never hidden or stripped of their text. What this setting controls is whether someone who may not see where the cave is gets told which documents point at it.
messaging.revealAssociations: Show attachments of protected caves to everyone who can read them
messaging.revealAssociationsHint: Turning this on never reveals a position: following the link still gives the protected view. A photo carrying its own capture point stays unpaired with a protected cave either way, because pairing the two would place the cave.
messaging.secretStored: A password is stored. Leave blank to keep it.
messaging.acceptInvalidCertificateHint: Only for an internal relay with a self-signed certificate. It removes the protection on the password above.
messaging.mailInactive: No mail server configured. Messages are written to the server log instead of being sent.
messaging.smsInactive: No SMS gateway configured. Texts are written to the server log instead of being sent.
messaging.smsIntro: Any gateway that accepts an HTTP request will work. Use {to}, {text} and {from} in the URL or body; each is escaped for you.
messaging.smsAuthHint: Sent as the Authorization header, for example "Basic ..." or "Bearer ...".
messaging.testNotConfigured: Configure and save the channel first.
messaging.sendConfirmation: Send a confirmation message when an account is created
messaging.requireConfirmed: Require a confirmed address to sign in
messaging.requireConfirmedHint: Accounts that have not confirmed their address will be refused at sign-in and offered a new confirmation message.
messaging.requireConfirmedInert: Has no effect until a mail server is configured — otherwise nobody could ever confirm.
messaging.needsMail: Needs a mail server before anyone can use it.
messaging.needsSms: Needs an SMS gateway before anyone can use it.
messaging.smsWeakest: The weakest of the three: a number can be moved to another SIM by persuading the mobile operator.

documentTypes.schemaHint: Leave empty for a kind that asks for nothing. Only flat text, number, yes/no and choice fields appear on the form.

documentTypes.codeTaken: Another kind already uses that code.
